FAIR-bioHeaders (FHR, see the `specification`_) puts provenance metadata in a header at the top of a data file: who made the genome assembly, annotation or protein set, from which organism, version, accession, license, the files it was derived from, and a checksum. The header lines start with ``;~`` in FASTA and ``#~`` in GFA and GFF3, before the first record, so the data itself is not changed. Headers follow the FHR schema for genome assemblies, FHP for protein FASTA and FHGFF3 for GFF3 annotation.
The checksum (SHA-512/256 of the whole file, header included, with a placeholder in place of the checksum itself) lets anyone check that neither the data nor the metadata has changed. Any change to the sequence, annotation or metadata needs a new checksum: recombine the file.

**Datatypes and other tools**
Galaxy detects FASTA on upload only when the first line starts with ``>``, so a FASTA file with a header is not detected as FASTA: set its datatype to ``fasta`` (or ``fasta.gz``) by hand.
Many FASTA tools reject a file with text before the first record, and some read the header as sequence. Remove the header with the **FAIR-bioHeaders strip** tool before passing the file to such a tool. The `tool compatibility`_ survey lists the results for the tools tested so far. In GFA and GFF3 the header lines are comments, which those formats allow; none of the GFA and GFF3 tools in the survey had problems with them.
Compressed (``.gz``) inputs give compressed outputs, written as BGZF (a form of gzip that htslib tools can index).
